title: Container Bookings: Goodwill Waivers of Booking Fees
content:
The Container Bookings desk can, within limits, cancel a fee on a booking as a gesture of goodwill. This page states which fees qualify and on what terms.

## Clauses in force

**Fees that can be waived.** Only entries coded as a cancellation fee, a no-show fee, a late shipping-instruction fee, a late VGM fee, an amendment fee, a change-of-destination fee or a customer roll fee can be waived. Goodwill never reaches ocean freight, bunker adjustment, terminal handling, the peak season surcharge, the equipment imbalance surcharge, the manual booking fee or the premium paid for a loading guarantee.

**Whole entries only.** A waiver cancels the entire fee entry it refers to, never a portion. It is written as an entry coded as a waiver, carrying the full amount of that fee entry.

**Amount limit.** The amount of the fee entry must be no greater than the desk's waiver authority for the product.

**Yearly quota.** Over the trailing 365 days the customer must have received fewer goodwill waivers than the product's quota. They are counted across every booking of the customer, taking entries coded as a waiver whose date falls within the 365 calendar days ending on the waiver date, both ends included; premium refunds are left out of the count. The comparison uses the quota of the product of the booking that carries the fee.

**Request period.** The customer must ask no later than the product's request period, in calendar days, after the date the fee was entered. The period ends on the fee's entry date moved forward by that many calendar days, regardless of the time of day, and a request made on that last day is inside it.

**Once per entry.** A fee entry can be waived one time only.

All of these are established from the line's charge records for the booking and the customer, not from the customer's recollection.

## Clauses no longer in force

- The opening grant, under which the desk could waive a single fee entry as goodwill at the verified customer's request with nothing further required, is no longer in force as the full statement of the desk's power; for customer roll fee entries it has been superseded by the current goodwill basis for those fees, which adds conditions.
- The closing sentence, under which a fee failing any of these conditions stayed payable and could not be reduced by the desk, is no longer in force in that wording; it has been superseded by the corresponding sentence of the current goodwill basis for customer roll fees.

## Request period boundary (hypothetical)

A fee entered on day F under a product with a 45-day request period can be waived on a request made on day F plus 45; a request on day F plus 46 is too late.

## Quota illustration (hypothetical)

Under an invented quota of 2, a customer with one goodwill waiver in the last 365 days and one premium refund in the same period has a count of 1 and may still receive a waiver; a customer with two goodwill waivers may not.

superseded_clauses: The desk may waive a single fee row as goodwill at the verified customer's request.
A fee that fails any of these conditions stays payable, and the desk has no authority to reduce it.
